author: Penry Buckley
description:
Follow live updates

Social media companies compelled to provide information under changes to minimum age ban, Albanese says

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, says social media companies have already been compelled to provide information to the eSafety commissioner following amendments to social media minimum legislation this month.

It was never going to be perfect, but in the legislation that we passed just in the last sitting fortnight, I can tell you … that already the eSafety Commissioner has used that strengthening of the laws to require some of the social media organisations to provide information to it, so they’ve already been compelled
title: News live: Taylor pledges ‘one of the biggest immigration cuts in Australian history’; tributes for Victorian Greens MP Tim Read

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Ruling latest step in legal fight over medically fragile child born after surrogate rejected couple’s request for abortion

The Texas supreme court has decided that the month-old infant that surrogate McKenna West gave birth to can be relocated to Los Angeles, a Thursday ruling that came weeks after a California court had recognized the biological parents’ custody rights.

“Sustaining the life of the medically fragile child is the paramount concern in this time-sensitive matter,” the court wrote in a Thursday order, referring to the baby’s rare severe heart defect. West had attempted to block the biological parents from removing the child from Texas and taking him to a hospital in Los Angeles where the couple live.

Continue reading...
title: Baby born via surrogate can leave Texas for treatment in California, court rules

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Arson attacks related to illegal tobacco trade are also causing revenue and reputation problems for neighbouring businesses

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Small businesses located near tobacconists are being denied insurance or priced out of coverage as rising arson attacks turn neighbouring shops into collateral damage.

The problem has intensified after a spate of firebombings, which includes a recent Melbourne blaze that destroyed a Richmond tobacco retailer and nearly a dozen neighbouring shops, requiring 80 firefighters to contain.
title: As tobacconist firebombings intensify in Melbourne, nearby stores are being denied insurance

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Premier Ben Carroll vows to legislate new form of manslaughter and increase maximum penalty for rape to life imprisonment

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A re-elected Victorian Labor government will create two new Australian-first offences aimed at closing “loopholes” it says have allowed perpetrators of family violence to escape punishment.

On Sunday, the premier, Ben Carroll, will announce an election commitment to legislate a new form of manslaughter covering cases in which a person takes their own life as a result of family violence, as well as a new offence covering perpetrators abandoning a victim in need of medical care.
title: Victorian Labor promises new offences to close domestic and family violence ‘loopholes’

author: Edward Helmore
description:
President said he was banning MS Now, CNN and Politico journalists, saying of their coverage: ‘You get sick of it.’

News outlets MS Now and CNN said their journalists were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday morning, a day after Donald Trump said he would ban them ,and the website Politico from the executive branch complex.

MS Now said a reporter and a cameraman had been denied access and had their White House press passes confiscated by the US Secret Service at a security gate outside the West Wing. CNN reported that its reporter Betsy Klein was also denied access and had her press pass seized too.

Continue reading...
title: MS Now and CNN say their reporters were denied access to White House after Trump media ban

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
The president has threatened to block renovations and suggested the landmark could be demolished after courts ruled against his bid to rename it

More than half a century later, the potential death knell came just after 4.30pm on Tuesday with a perfunctory announcement on the public address system: “The centre is now closed to the public. title: Trump’s battle to rename the Kennedy Center has put its future at risk

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
The report highlights deep divides between low- and middle- income, a disparity that dates back decades

A new report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reaffirms that adults are more likely to eat fresh fruits and vegetables as their income increases.

The data brief comes as Republican cuts to food assistance programs, colloquially called “food stamps”, have led enrollment to “plummet”. Changes to US dietary guidelines, led by health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, have also made a government-recommended diet more expensive. A new
title: Likelihood of eating fresh produce increases with income for US adults, new CDC report shows

author: Eric Berger
description:
Acts of ‘familicide’ have increased dramatically this year – in the US, the killer is more likely to have easy access to a gun

The US is often known globally for its shocking levels of violence, but acts of “family annihilation” or “familicide” rank among the most disturbing of crimes.

They occur when an assailant kills four or more of their own family members and often see the killer also kill themselves. These types of crime have increased dramatically this year, according to data from Northeastern University.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Way too many guns around’: experts say firearm access key factor in spate of US family killings

author: Danny Lavelle
description:
Co-owner of Manchester United says Britain is in decline because of high taxes and immigration

The co-owner of Manchester United Sir Jim Ratcliffe has described the UK as being a country “on the slide” from the days when it had “the greatest empire in the world.”

Ratcliffe, who founded petrochemicals giant Ineos, and has resided in Monaco, which has a relaxed tax regime, since 2020, said Britain is in decline because of high taxes and immigration.

Continue reading...
title: Jim Ratcliffe says the UK is a country ‘on the slide’

author: Sammy Gecsoyler
description:
Emergency services called to Grand Burstin hotel in Folkestone, where a fire is believed to have started in the basement

Hundreds of people have been evacuated from a hotel in Folkestone after a large fire broke out overnight.

Just after 1am on Saturday, emergency services were called to the Grand Burstin hotel in The Harbour, Folkestone, where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent fire and rescue service said.

Continue reading...
title: Hundreds evacuated after fire breaks out at seaside hotel in Kent

author: David Smith and agencies
description:
Demonstrators gathered outside the building in Washington, after the president was spotted holding a placard that read: ‘Kennedy Center DEMOLIS ...’

On Friday evening thousands of protesters gathered outside the Kennedy Center in view of the marble facade that remained concealed by scaffolding and tarpaulins, to protest Donald Trump’s plans for the facility and express alarm that he might make good on his threat to tear down the institution.

Crowding streets in the Foggy Bottom area of Washington and locking down traffic as they walked, many carried signs, as they joined in the “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” protest. Some wore costumes and booed when the president was mentioned during the program.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands protest closure of the Kennedy Center amid fears Trump is set to demolish the institution

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
The FBI says Daejon Love and his alleged accomplice, Taylor Chan, defrauded women they met on dating apps out of $1.3m

At least 35 additional women have come forward with fraud allegations against Daejon Love, the man accused last month of masquerading as a San Francisco 49ers player and wealthy investor, the FBI announced on Friday. Federal authorities had previously said Love conned more than two dozen women, many of whom he met on dating apps, out of $1.3m.

Love, 35, and alleged accomplice Taylor Chan, 18, who posed as his financial adviser, were arrested in August and have been charged with wire fraud.

Continue reading...
title: More than 35 woman come forward in case against fake 49ers player accused of fraud
